Chapter 7: Safeguarding Professional and Personal Ethics.
Let’s dive right in. Building on what we’ve just talked about, it’s so important to think about how we keep our ethical standards strong—both at work and in our personal lives—especially when the world around us gets turbulent.
In tough times, like during political upheaval, you might feel pressure to bend your values. Maybe it’s for your own safety, convenience, or even personal gain. But that’s when staying true to your ethics matters most.
Think about professionals—judges, doctors, journalists, teachers. Authoritarian regimes often target these folks because their cooperation gives unjust systems a sense of legitimacy. But when they stand firm and stick to their ethical codes, they become a real line of defense against the abuse of power.
Imagine a judge who simply refuses to enforce an unfair law. Or a doctor who treats every patient equally, no matter the risk. By doing this, they not only honor their profession, but also protect people who might otherwise be left vulnerable.
Now, on a more personal level, living ethically is about refusing to take part in, or benefit from, systems that hurt others. Maybe you’re offered a promotion that asks you to do something you know isn’t right. Or there’s a chance to profit from a practice that discriminates against people. Walking away from those choices can be tough—and yes, sometimes it’ll cost you. But by doing so, you help keep society’s moral fabric intact, and you set an example others can follow.
So, how do you actually safeguard your ethics? Here are a few things to keep in mind:
First, know your code. Be crystal clear about what your profession expects, and what you personally believe in.
Second, refuse to participate in injustice. Even if you’re under pressure, say no to actions that go against your principles.
And finally, support ethical colleagues. Stand together with people who are doing the right thing, and build networks where you’ve got each other’s backs.
Remember, ethical resistance isn’t always about making grand, dramatic gestures. Most of the time, it’s about the choices you make every single day. By holding the line—no matter how small the situation might seem—you help stop wrongdoing from becoming “just the way things are.”
